passage: Note from Vinita, playgroup teacher. At pick-up today I saw Rafiq's mother tell him no more juice. Rafiq dropped to the floor, screamed and kicked his heels. She did not raise her voice. She crouched beside him: "You are so angry. You wanted more juice. No more today." She waited. When his crying eased, she offered water or the picture book. He took the book and sniffled. I shared with her how steady this looked from where I stood.

qa.q: What did Rafiq's mother offer when his crying eased?
qa.a: She offered water or the picture book.

qa.q: What was Rafiq feeling when he dropped to the floor and kicked?
qa.a: He was full of rage and disappointment. He has no words for it yet, so it came out through his body.

qa.q: How did Rafiq's mother hold the limit while helping him?
qa.a: She kept her voice calm, named the feeling, waited out the storm and stayed firm that there was no more juice, while offering a safe alternative.

qa.q: How might Vinita's comment feel to Rafiq's mother after a public tantrum?
qa.a: It may come as relief to hear that someone saw her steadiness and not only the scene. That encouragement helps her repeat the same approach.

grounding: Told no, the toddler screams and drops to the floor; the parent holds the limit, names the feeling and offers an alternative.

passage:
Monday. "No sweets now," Maria said. Vishal, two, screamed and dropped to the floor. Maria shouted back, and he screamed louder.

Wednesday. "No sweets now." Vishal wailed. Maria sat nearby. "You're so cross. You wanted it." She waited.

Two weeks later. "No sweets. Want a banana?" Vishal cried a bit, then took the banana.

qa.q: What did Maria offer instead of sweets two weeks later?
What was Vishal feeling when he dropped to the floor?
qa.a: Vishal felt a rage he had no words for, after being told no.

qa.q: What changed Maria's approach, and why did it help?
qa.a: She held the limit gently, named his feeling, let the storm pass and offered a safe alternative instead of shouting back.

qa.q: How might Maria feel two weeks later when Vishal takes the banana?
qa.a: Maria likely feels relieved and more confident.

grounding: Shows a toddler raging when told no, and a parent learning to hold the limit gently, name the feeling and offer an alternative.

passage:
In the Amritsar market, Deepak, two, grabbed a toy drum. "No, beta. Not today," Jasleen said.

Deepak screamed and dropped to the floor, kicking.

Jasleen crouched beside him. "You're angry. You wanted the drum." She waited while he cried.

When he quieted, she held out her keys. "Want to shake these?"

Deepak jingled the keys all the way home.

qa.q: What did Deepak grab in the market?
Why did Deepak scream and kick?
qa.a: Deepak felt furious and had no words for his disappointment at being told no.
She held the limit gently, named his anger, let the storm pass and then offered a safe alternative, her keys.

qa.q: How might passers-by in the market see the tantrum?
qa.a: Some may see it as naughtiness, while Jasleen understands it as big feelings with no words yet.

grounding: Shows a toddler's rage at being told no, met with a gentle limit, named feelings and a safe alternative.
